blogs.title: LSTMs Are Back? What xLSTM Means for the Future of Language Models
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the paper’s big claim: that upgraded LSTMs can once again compete with Transformers and modern state space models. This post would explain the historical rise of LSTMs, why Transformers overtook them, and how xLSTM revisits the old architecture with modern scaling techniques to make it relevant for today’s large language models.

blogs.title: The Three Problems with Classic LSTMs—and How xLSTM Fixes Them
blogs.description: A breakdown of the core motivation behind xLSTM. This post would explain, in plain language, the three limitations of standard LSTMs identified by the paper: difficulty revising memories, limited storage capacity, and weak parallelization. It would then show how exponential gating, new memory designs, and updated architecture choices directly address those issues.

blogs.title: Exponential Gating Explained: The Secret Sauce Behind xLSTM
blogs.description: A deep but approachable explainer focused on one of the paper’s main innovations: replacing standard sigmoid-style gating with exponential gating plus normalization and stabilization. The post would use intuitive examples to show why this helps the model revise earlier memory decisions and track important information more effectively over long sequences.

blogs.title: From Scalar Memory to Matrix Memory: Why mLSTM Thinks More Like Retrieval
blogs.description: A post centered on the mLSTM variant and its matrix-based memory. It would explain how moving from a single compressed memory value to a matrix memory lets the model store and retrieve key-value information more like attention systems do, while still keeping linear sequence complexity. The article would highlight why this especially helps with rare tokens and associative recall.

blogs.title: sLSTM vs. mLSTM: Two New Kinds of Memory for Long-Context AI
blogs.description: A comparison-style post that introduces the two main xLSTM building blocks: sLSTM and mLSTM. It would explain what each one is good at, why one emphasizes memory mixing and state tracking while the other emphasizes storage capacity and parallelism, and how combining them in one architecture gives xLSTM its strength.

blogs.title: Can xLSTM Beat Transformers on Long Context? What the Results Actually Show
blogs.description: A results-focused summary of the experiments, aimed at readers who want the practical takeaway without reading the full paper. This post would cover how xLSTM performs on language modeling, long-context extrapolation, downstream tasks, and scaling laws, and why the authors believe it can remain competitive as models grow larger.
